title: Skillet White Bean and Zucchini Pizza Bake
intro: This savory one-pan meal delivers plenty of vegetables and plant-based protein for lasting fullness. Creamy navy beans replace a refined flour crust, providing a comforting, high-fiber base for classic pizza flavors.

ingredients.name: Zucchini
ingredients.canonical_name: Squash, summer, zucchini, includes skin, raw

ingredients.name: Cremini mushrooms
ingredients.canonical_name: Mushrooms, brown, italian, or crimini, raw

ingredients.name: No-salt-added navy beans
ingredients.canonical_name: Beans, navy, mature seeds, canned, no salt added

ingredients.name: No-salt-added canned crushed tomatoes
ingredients.canonical_name: Tomatoes, crushed, canned, no salt added

instructions: Heat the olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sauté the zucchini and mushrooms in the skillet until softened and lightly browned, 5 to 7 minutes.
Stir the garlic powder, dried oregano, navy beans, and crushed tomatoes into the skillet.
Reduce the heat to medium and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly, 3 to 4 minutes.
Remove the skillet from the heat and sprinkle the shredded mozzarella and grated Parmesan evenly over the top.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake until the cheese is melted and bubbling, 4 to 5 minutes.
variation: Swap the cremini mushrooms for diced green bell peppers.
conservation: Keeps 3 days refrigerated; reheat in the microwave.
validation_warnings: Stage 4 coverage: 'Extra-virgin olive oil': [748608] Oil, olive, extra virgin has no USDA value for fiber_g, protein_g (which would be summed as zero) — switched to [171413] Oil, olive, salad or cooking.

Stage 4 qualifier: 'No-salt-added navy beans': the recipe uses a canned product but the match is cooked from dry (different water content, so a different weight basis). No candidate in the USDA shortlist satisfies it, so [173746] Beans, navy, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt was kept — treat this ingredient's contribution as an over-statement.
cholesterol_mg: partial data — 25% of recipe weight has no USDA value for it.

[taste_coherence] The recipe includes over 1.5 lbs of watery vegetables (zucchini, mushrooms), beans, and tomatoes, but specifies zero added salt or black pepper, relying entirely on a small amount of cheese for seasoning. This will result in a very bland, unbalanced base. Fix: Add 1/8 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper in step 3 to draw out the mushroom moisture and properly season the vegetables. This adds ~145 mg sodium per serving, keeping the total (450 mg) safely below the 550 mg chapter ceiling.
